title: Mets’ Jared Young knocked out after taking knee to head in ‘terrifying’ collision | MLB | The Guardian
description: The New York first baseman was carted off the field in the sixth inning after he was struck on the head by the knee of pitched Nolan McLean
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The New York first baseman was carted off the field in the sixth inning after he was struck on the head by the knee of pitched Nolan McLean
Content: Jared Young is brought off the field on a stretcher.Photograph: Seth Wenig/APView image in fullscreenJared Young is brought off the field on a stretcher.Photograph: Seth Wenig/APMLBMets’ Jared Young knocked out after taking knee to head in ‘terrifying’ collisionFirst baseman ran into teammate McLean in sixth inningYoung has concussion symptoms, negative CT scanManager says ‘scariest outcomes’ were avoidedAssociated PressFri 18 Sep 2026 07.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNew York Mets first baseman Jared Young was carted off the field in the sixth inning of Thursday night’s 3-0 loss to Philadelphia after he was knocked out when struck on the head by a knee of pitcher Nolan McLean as the two converged on Justin Crawford’s slow grounder.Mets manager Andy Green said a CT scan at a hospital was negative. Young had concussion symptoms and full use of his extremities, according to Green.“It was a terrifying moment on a baseball field,” Green said. “Took him a while to come to. It was a really scary collision.”Mets fans celebrate home run against own team as returning hero Alonso goes yardRead moreWith the Phillies ahead 1-0, McLean broke to first on contact and Young initially moved back toward the bag. McLean briefly paused, at which point Young reached for the ball with his right hand as he tried to keep a foot on the base. McLean resumed running then collided with Young’s head, tripping over the first baseman as Crawford crossed the bag. Young fell face first to the ground and was motionless.“It was scary to sit there and just know that he wasn’t with us in that moment,” Mets shortstop Francisco Lindor said. “He was just somewhere else.”Green and an athletic trainer immediately ran out from the dugout, and a cart was summoned.McLean put his hands on his knees and bent down as all the Mets on the field gathered near Young. Catcher Francisco Alvarez appeared to be praying and members of both teams looked on from the dugouts. Philadelphia’s Alec Bohm took a knee next to third base.“It was weird. You couldn’t tell what happened,” said Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly, a former big league first baseman. “I heard it was bad. Hopefully the kid’s all right.”When Young came to, Green said the first baseman asked: “What happened?”Young was immobilized on the cart and flashed a thumbs up before the cart disappeared behind the left-center field fence.“He’s had a CT scan. Results have come back negative,” Green said. “So in that sense it’s very positive. Still experiencing real concussion symptoms right now but has full use of his extremities and feels at this point in time like we’ve avoided the scariest outcomes.”Young, a 31-year-old in his first full big league season, has established himself as a regular first baseman by hitting .266 with nine homers and 39 RBIs in 103 games. He missed six weeks with a left knee injury.“He’s somebody we all respect and appreciate and have love for,” Lindor said. “He’s been a big part of our team this whole year.”McLean was shaken by the collision. He remained in the game and threw a called third strike past Garrett Stubbs, ending the inning. He was removed by Green for reliever Tobias Myers at the start of the seventh.“Probably should have made a better decision not even letting him get the next hitter but he was still strong enough to do it and got back out there and did it,” Green said. “I think the humanity hit him pretty hard right there.”Explore more on these topicsMLBBaseballUS sportsNew York MetsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Brentford blitz Chelsea as Fábio Carvalho caps stunning second-half display | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Brentford won 3-0 against Chelsea via second-half goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Brentford won 3-0 against Chelsea via second-half goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho
Content: Jaidon Anthony (left) and Igor Thiago – two of Brentford goalscorers – after the opener against Chelsea.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersView image in fullscreenJaidon Anthony (left) and Igor Thiago – two of Brentford goalscorers – after the opener against Chelsea.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersPremier LeagueBrentford blitz Chelsea as Fábio Carvalho caps stunning second-half displayJonathan Wilsonat the Gtech Community StadiumFri 18 Sep 2026 17.12 EDTLast modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 19.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThose early-season thoughts thatChelseamight be the team best-placed to challenge Arsenal are beginning to look extremely over-optimistic. The two chaotic wins with which they began were always difficult to read: they might have been useful points picked up on the way to a more solid structure, or they might have represented evidence of significant problems. After three games without a win, and 12 goals conceded in five games this season, it’s beginning to look like the latter.At the final whistle, Keith Andrews tipped his head back and roared at the sky, celebrating Brentford’s first home win over Chelsea since 1938. They remain unbeaten, coherent and disciplined, and moved up to third in the table. The comparison is impossible not to draw: as one side flail in an orgy of structured spending, their far less wealthy neighbours thrive with a clear plan and sense of direction. “It was a performance I felt was bubbling,” said Andrews. “I could see it in the players’ eyes over the last two days. They were very focused, very determined.”Brentford v Chelsea: Premier League – liveRead moreSuch is the state of perpetual flux at Chelsea that the usual homilies about the benefits of stability always seem a little redundant when applied to them. With 11 new signings this summer maintaining the sense of the club as a trading hub, learning the names of everybody in the dressing room has probably been a greater priority than worrying too much about boardroom wrangling. But, still, their first game since Todd Boehly and Mark Walteragreed to sell their 12.8% stakein the club to the major shareholder Clearlake Capital felt significant. At the very least, a more harmonious boardroom should be beneficial.Boehly, the great disruptor, who arrived blithely telling English football it was doing everything wrong, has departed having achieved very little other than splurging £300m on players who didn’t fit and giving Raheem Sterling a £325,000-a-week contract in his shambolic spell as de facto sporting director. Four years on, after 60 arrivals, do Chelsea look any more like title challengers than they did then? It was, in truth, very hard to say what this looked like, other than a team that is every much still under construction. Jordan Henderson made his full Chelsea debut at his former club, while Danny Welbeck, Pep Chavarría and Valentín Barco made their first league starts.Barco, whose overenthusiastic celebrations after Argentina’s winner against England at the World Cup earned him a post-match slap from Jude Bellingham, was booed with impressive consistency from the home fans. The lesson was clear: if you’re going to be a major irritant while in possession of a distinctive shock of hair the colour of burnished copper, there will be consequences. Emí Martínez was jeered as well for the crime of being Argentinian. Henderson, by contrast, was treated relatively gently, his booing as a returnee more sporadic and muted, tending to the perfunctory.View image in fullscreenJaidon Anthony rises to head Brentford in front.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersThe pattern for Chelsea was a familiar one: a fast start, fading to something a little scratchier. The opening, for the second successive game, did not produce an early goal, although Pedro Neto would have given them a ninth-minute lead had it not been for a sharp save from Caoimhín Kelleher.“We have dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality in the second half,” said Xabi Alonso. “We have not been able to keep our level. When you lose shape you are out of control. To be able to understand and know what it takes to be competing to the end, it’s a process and it takes time.”The longer the game went on, the less assured Chelsea looked and a Brentford opener arrived just after the hour. Perhaps inevitably, it came from a dead ball; the stats had suggested that Brentford this season had been creating significantly more chances from set plays than they had converted. As modern corner routines go it seemed very straightforward, Jannik Schuster climbing above the diminutive Barco to head Mikkel Damsgaard’s corner back across goal, where Jaidon Anthony nodded in from close range, his first goal since his summer move from Burnley.View image in fullscreenFábio Carvalho fires Brentford into a three-goal lead in injury time.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersChelsea belatedly applied some pressure but, although the final minutes were played largely in the Brentford half, they created little beyond corners, as Brentford maintained their composure and structure.The second goal arrived seven minutes from time. Damsgaard, perhaps the tidiest player in the league, led the break, playing in Kevin Schade. Martínez saved his side-footed effort but Igor Thiago guided an awkwardly bouncing ball inside the post for his first goal of the season. Fábio Carvalho made it 3-0 in added time, slamming in a cross from Schade, who had been left inexplicably unmarked on the left after a long throw was half-cleared.As Brentford begin to consider that European qualification is a real possibility, Chelsea remain what they have been since the takeover: a work in progress – and, particularly at the back, it feels that progress has a long way to run.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueBrentfordChelseamatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Trent Alexander-Arnold recalled by England but with a warning from Thomas Tuchel | England | The Guardian
description: Thomas Tuchel has told Trent ­Alexander-Arnold he must bring defensive solidity to the England squad after giving him a surprise recall for the upcoming Nations League matches
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Thomas Tuchel has told Trent ­Alexander-Arnold he must bring defensive solidity to the England squad after giving him a surprise recall for the upcoming Nations League matches
Content: Trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the England fold.Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenTrent Alexander-Arnold is back in the England fold.Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockEnglandTrent Alexander-Arnold recalled by England but with a warning from Thomas TuchelReal Madrid player must help improve defensive solidityScott, Hall, Lewis-Skelly and Calvert-Lewin selectedDavid HytnerFri 18 Sep 2026 14.08 EDTFirst published on Fri 18 Sep 2026 05.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel has toldTrent Alexander-Arnoldhe must bring defensive solidity to the England squad after giving him a surprise recall for the upcoming Nations League matches.The head coach has selected the Real Madrid right-back only once before – for the games against Andorra and Senegal in June last year. Tuchel made headlines when he did so by urging Alexander-Arnold to focus on the defensive side of his game or risk a slip that could undermine the team’s World Cup campaign.‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football cultureRead moreTuchel used him as a 64th-minute substitute against Andorra and Alexander-Arnold was out of the picture by the timeEnglandwent to North America for the tournament. He is now back, despite starting only three of Madrid’s seven matches this season and largely going under the radar with his performances. Tuchel’s message to him has not changed.“He has to, it’s necessary,” Tuchel said when asked whether Alexander-Arnold offered enough defensively. “My conviction is that he will but he has no choice.”Tuchel continues to see Alexander-Arnold, who is famed for the range of his passing, as a right-back rather than a midfielder. The head coach has previously said he has Tino Livramento and Jarell Quansah ahead of Alexander-Arnold in the right-back pecking order. He has named both of them in the squad for the games against Spain (home), Czechia (home and away) and Croatia (away).Quick GuideEngland's squadShowGoalkeepers:Jordan Pickford, James Trafford, Jason Steele.Defenders:Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarrod Branthwaite, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Guéhi, Lewis Hall, Ezri Konsa, Tino Livramento, Nico O’Reilly, Jarell Quansah.Midfielders:Elliot Anderson, Jude Bellingham, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Alex Scott.Forwards:Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Eberechi Eze, Anthony Gordon, Harry Kane, Rio Ngumoha, Marcus Rashford, Morgan Rogers, Bukayo Saka.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Tuchel has been unable to include his first-choice right-back, Reece James, or Djed Spence, who can operate in either full-back position, because of injuries. Ben White is also injured; Tuchel said he would have considered him. The centre-half Ezri Konsa, who is in the squad, has played at right-back.Tuchel said he had spoken to Alexander-Arnold to tell him he would not go to the World Cup but had not called him this time. “He heard the good news over the nomination,” he said. “I am not sure a lot of things have changed. I know what he is capable of. I know about his talent. I know what he is saying: that he is desperate to play for England and he will fight for his shirt. It’s a long camp and it’s a good moment to show up. It’s a chance for Trent to claim what he feels is his – his place on the right side. So here we go.”Graphic showing minutes played for England under Thomas Tuchel by members of this squadAlexander-Arnold was the headline selection on a day when Tuchel gave further recalls to Jarrad Branthwaite, Lewis Hall, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Alex Scott, Cole Palmer and Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He also included Rio Ngumoha. Dean Henderson, John Stones, Dan Burn and Jordan Henderson miss out because of injury. Noni Madueke, Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney have been dropped.Tuchel overlooked Levi Colwill, Adam Wharton, Phil Foden and Morgan Gibbs-White. Nor was there a recall for Harry Maguire. Tuchel gave the defender hope of involvement at the World Cup when he selected him against Uruguay and Japan in March before he ignored him for the tournament. It drew an outspoken response, Maguire using social media to pronounce himself “shocked and gutted”. His mother, Zoe, said she was “disgusted” by the decision.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Of Maguire’s reaction, Tuchel said: “I will not hold it against him for the rest of his life because I’m not that type of person. I can forget easily and quickly. But I didn’t like it and it doesn’t help.”Tuchel said he had not spoken to Maguire since.Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelTrent Alexander-ArnoldNations LeaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Harry Kane smashes record for fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals in 98th game | Bayern Munich | The Guardian
description: Harry Kane beat the 49-year-old record for the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals by 31 matches as Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Harry Kane beat the 49-year-old record for the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals by 31 matches as Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0
Content: Harry Kane celebrates scoring Bayern Munich’s fourth goal, his second of the match, against Union Berlin.Photograph: Anna Szilágyi/EPAView image in fullscreenHarry Kane celebrates scoring Bayern Munich’s fourth goal, his second of the match, against Union Berlin.Photograph: Anna Szilágyi/EPABayern MunichHarry Kane smashes record for fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals in 98th gameKane double helps Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0Dieter Müller’s record of 129 games had stood since 1977Press AssociationFri 18 Sep 2026 18.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHarry Kane smashed the 49-year-old record for the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals in Bayern Munich’s 7-0 victory over Union Berlin, his 98th league game for the club.Cologne’s Dieter Müller set the previous mark in 1977, but it took him 129 matches and, with the England captain scoring at better than a goal a game, a new record had been inevitable for some time. Since his arrival in 2023 Kane had been averaging aBundesligagoal every 78.5 minutes and has now scored 152 in 154 appearances in all competitions, including 61 in 51 games last term.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHarry Kane and Alessia Russo among nominees for this year’s Ballon d’OrRead moreHe blasted home a 39th-minute penalty to take the record before nodding in a Michael Olise cross early in the second half to send Bayern top of the table before the other weekend matches.The feat stole the spotlight from Olise, who scored his first Bayern hat-trick, and Jamal Musiala, who also scored a goal worthy of winning any game.“I’m very proud to have now scored 100 and 101 Bundesliga goals. I haven’t been around that long. I’ve loved every second of it,” Kane told Sky Germany. “With Michael, Lucho [Luis Díaz] and Jamal I naturally get chances and today was no exception.“So I just want to thank the team, the club, the coach, and the staff – everyone who has helped me achieve this. Let’s keep going like this. Scoring more goals in games is obviously a big step. Of course, there have been many important goals among them. I can only say that I’m enjoying every minute of it. Just like today.”Explore more on these topicsBayern MunichHarry KaneUnion BerlinBundesligaEuropean club footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Women’s Super League: Lauren Hemp hits double as Manchester City see off lively Liverpool | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Manchester City maintained their 100% start with the England star scoring twice but Liverpool threatened a shock before a 4-2 win for hosts
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Manchester City maintained their 100% start with the England star scoring twice but Liverpool threatened a shock before a 4-2 win for hosts
Content: Manchester City’s Lauren Hemp celebrates scoring their fourth goal as Khiara Keating looks to the ground.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenManchester City’s Lauren Hemp celebrates scoring their fourth goal as Khiara Keating looks to the ground.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersWomen's Super LeagueWomen’s Super League: Lauren Hemp hits double as Manchester City see off lively LiverpoolTom GarryFri 18 Sep 2026 16.10 EDTLast modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 19.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester City continued their winning start to the new Women’s Super League season but the defending champions needed a 90th-minute own goal from Grace Fisk to help them edge past an ever-improving Liverpool side after an entertaining game in which Lauren Hemp scored twice.Fisk inadvertently turned Grace Clinton’s dangerous cross into her own net to put City 3-2 up and then – with Liverpool searching for an equaliser and committing players forward deep in stoppage time – Hemp added another on the counterattack to make it 4-2 and widen the margin of victory, but that slightly masked how well the visitors had played.Gareth Taylor – against his former side – will have taken significant encouragement from his Liverpool team’s performance, on a night when they made the league leaders dig deep.Laura Kaminski relishing trophy hunt at Brann after Crystal Palace ‘crash course’Read more“Playing that way, we believe we’ll win a lot of games this season,” Taylor told Sky Sports, as he praised his team’s effort. “What you saw was a more improved version of what we were towards the end of last season.”That certainly seemed the case. Nevertheless, the result ensured that City, who had already been the only WSL side who held a 100% winning record after the opening two rounds of games and now will certainly stay top of the table for at least another week, have still not dropped any points in home league fixtures since Andrée Jeglertz took charge in the summer of 2025.It had looked as though Jeglertz’s City were set for a routine evening when Hemp met Carlotta Wamser’s incisive inside ball and sent a controlled, low finish into the far bottom corner. It was Hemp’s first goal sincescoring for Englandin a victory over Spain in April, her first club goal since scoring in the FA Cup in February and her first WSL goal since last November’s Manchester derby.Moments after Hemp’s opening goal, with 13 minutes on the clock, the entire crowd rose to applaudthe late Matt Beard, the former Liverpool manager, in reference to the year 2013, when he won the first of two consecutive WSL titles with Liverpool.Supporters of clubs across the WSL and WSL2 have been invited to applaud at the same time in games across this weekend, to mark a year since Beard’s death on 20 September 2025. He was a much-loved character and hugely successful coach at Liverpool, whose performance – particularly in the remainder of the first half – would have done him proud.View image in fullscreenVivien Endemann puts Liverpool 2-1 up against Manchester City.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAThe away side deservedly struck back and found themselves 2-1 up before the half-hour mark, as their pressing gave the defending champions a headache. First a misunderstanding between Wamser and Alex Greenwood allowed Vivien Endemann to set up Alice Bergström for the equaliser, which she calmly tucked past Ayaka Yamashita.Soon afterwards, after City failed to clear a cross, Endemann – who had opened her Liverpool account with a debut goal at Charlton on the opening weekend – fired in a shot that Yamashita got a hand to but could only help into the net.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFrom Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World CupRead moreKhadija Shaw struck a post from a difficult angle after rounding Khiara Keating, but Shaw eventually did equalise after a goalkeeping error shortly before half-time. Keating – returning to face her former club after her summer move to Liverpool – did well to block Hemp’s strike but was unable to prevent the ball trickling into the path of the onrushing Shaw, who gratefully poked home.Keating impressed in the second half with a fine reaction save, keeping out a Shaw effort that had looked destined for the top corner at her near post. But the hosts began to build pressure and the introduction of the lively Clinton inside the final 15 minutes boosted their attacking threat.Her near-post cross proved too difficult for Fisk to clear and – just as they did on countless occasions last term – City lived up to Jeglertz’s mantra of “we will find a way to win”, a message that has been imprinted on the walls of their training base.Jeglertz hinted at that again as he told Sky Sports: “I’m very pleased with the mentality of the group. They never stop believing, they keep on going and – in the end – we are winners.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueManchester City WomenLiverpool FC WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: We wanted to let Max Dowman bloom in the shadows but he has become hard to ignore | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: This most modern and well-honed of footballers will not be able to escape the spotlight in an age of constant scrutiny but looks equipped to handle it
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: This most modern and well-honed of footballers will not be able to escape the spotlight in an age of constant scrutiny but looks equipped to handle it
Content: Max Dowman’s excellence seems comfortable with itself.Illustration: Nathan DanielsView image in fullscreenMax Dowman’s excellence seems comfortable with itself.Illustration: Nathan DanielsArsenalWe wanted to let Max Dowman bloom in the shadows but he has become hard to ignoreBarney RonayThis most modern and well-honed of footballers will not be able to escape the spotlight in an age of constant scrutiny but looks equipped to handle itFri 18 Sep 2026 12.59 EDTLast modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 17.10 EDTShareThe poet Jorge Luis Borges wrote a famous short story about a society that had become so good at making maps, so obsessed with capturing every detail, that its rulers decided the only way to do the job right was to make a lifesize map of its entire empire, which could then be laid out across the actual land from coast to coast. Imagine a map of Britain the exact same size as Britain, showing every branch of Greggs, every nail bar, every vape shop in perfect detail. Only then can we really see what Britain looks like, by standing on a fake Britain laid over the top of actual Britain.Borges was writing in the 1940s, at a time when people were fascinated by the mechanised future, with its new forms of measuring out the world: the wireless, the 30mph motorcar, the rise of Big Tape Measure. And to be fair, the mega-map is a pretty accurate vision of our own fully networked present, a place where you can snoop around a village in Mozambique from your laptop in Egham, where no one ever stops committing acts of minute self-surveillance, even if they think they’re just searching “What is beetroot?” on the internet.‘They are very similar’: Arsenal’s Dowman reminds Merino of Lamine YamalRead moreBorges also hated football. “Soccer is popular because stupidity is popular,” he wrote, which probably seemed a bold statement at the time. But then Borges also didn’t live to see an episode of Wow Sports Premier League Breakfast at Breakfast with Roger McRoger and a puzzled Lee Trundle. After which, perhaps less of a surprise. But the process he describes is also a good description of what football is doing to itself. Endless data, endless analysis, no spaces or free air, matches that are just schematised movement. At times it can feel like football is out there laying a lifesize real-time map on top of itself.In Borges’s story, the land soon begins to decay beneath the massive map – which is reassessed by later generations as insane, pointless and stupid – and left to rot in the desert. We haven’t reached this point. Nobody is de-mapping football. But it does perhaps explain why everyone gets so excited when a talent emerges that seems to be playful and human, to exist outside the grid. And also why it has felt wrong to gush too soon about Max Dowman, to fear placing the hex on him. We know how this works. Here is a fluffy new thing. Let us break him. Let us heap pressure on his shoulders. Don’t talk about Max Dowman. Let Max Dowman exist, breathe, bloom in the shadows.So, Max Dowman then. It has become quite hard to ignore him. He was brilliantagainst Ipswich in midweek, and brilliant in a way that seems solid and real and comfortable with itself. Most obviously there were the two goals, both a perfect snapshot of why Dowman seems equipped to survive, more state‑of‑the‑art than some other young players we’ve burdened with expectation.The second goal is particularly good, five perfect little actions packed into six seconds of football.Arsenalhave the ball on the edge of the Ipswich box. Dowman shows for a pass, sees it’s going elsewhere, changes his mind, and makes a three-yard sprint to create space. Finally he has the physical capacity to control a bouncing ball in that sliver of space, to move his feet so much quicker than the nearest defender it looks like a glitch in the machine, and to finish in a way that involves sifting the options and timing the shot, all without breaking stride.View image in fullscreenMax Dowman leaves Cédric Kipré floundering to score his brilliant second, and Arsenal’s third, goal at Ipswich.Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/ShutterstockThe first goal is on his other side, and involves a more classical piece of one-on-one deception. This is the same defender: Cédric Kipré, 29 years old, came through Paris Saint-Germain’s youth system. Dowman walks through him with a micro-feint and a switch of feet, then reels off another hilariously understated finish, doing it all while a second defender is still gathering himself to lunge, like a man operating in a different time signature to everyone around him.This is the key point of difference, the ability to make everything stop, the fly-vision that means he sees what’s about to happen while everyone else is whirling about trying to read the charts, in the same way Lionel Messi (yes, sorry, sorry) always seems to have time to pass the ball into the net, like this is all a kickabout in a pair of sliders.Our way ofunderstanding young creative playershas often seemed to lag behind where the game actually is, to be driven by nostalgia for what this thing used to look like. I remember the excitement over the 18-year-old Jack Rodwell’s physicality at the exact moment physicality was no longer going to be a thing, like proudly unveiling the latest horse‑drawn train just as the Ford Model T rolls off the production line.Michael Owen was brilliant at 17, but he was mainly brilliant at running very fast in a straight line and smashing the ball into the net. Plus of course there was Wayne Rooney, who emerged a pale, unformed teenager composed entirely from energy drinks and white bread, out there making the game up on the fly, as though some urban foundling had come barrelling over the advert boards with a string of sausages still dangling from his mouth.The narrative around Rooney is that he lost this vital native quality. But Rooney adapted and survived, and clearly understood what he had to be a lot better than those of us watching. And even now creative players have to exist against this. Cole Palmer is exciting because he does surprising things that seem to be striking a blow for freedom, beauty and older people who struggle to make their email work. But his real challenge is to retain just enough of this while fitting the world around him.Dowman is a bit different. The things that make him stand out seem to speak very easily to how football is now. Being a modern creative footballer is not jinking runs, rasping drives or dribbling across a cabbage field in a pair of cowboy boots. It’s targeted energy, high-intensity semi-freedom. Lamine Yamal and Désiré Doué have the same fast-twitch foot and brain speed, the ability to operate in micro-moments, to see patterns just ahead of time. Dowman is 6ft tall and getting stronger. He won’t be kicked to pieces. He can repeat this without taking bites out of himself.There is still the issue of his youth. But maybe this doesn’t matter so much either. The world has changed. In the age of Rooney and Owen there was no care, no data, no softness. This is where the structures of modern football are an advantage. Dowman will be GPS’d to the last decimal point. Endless physical scientists will have a say on his output and stress levels.View image in fullscreenWayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as teenagers in an age of less data and less care.Photograph: PA Images/AlamyThe money is too big. The talent is too valuable. It also comes ready to plug and play. You don’t get to this level unless you can ingest systems and briefings. You’ve already been pressure-cooked and stress-tested. What you’re being asked to do in the orderly spaces of professional football is the same thing you were asked to do in the orderly spaces of academy football, just five levels up and with more people watching.Borges was anti-football because he saw it as inauthentic, the players no longer sports people but “actors in jerseys before the TV cameras”. And this is also fine, further evidence that boomer-dad nostalgia is one of the key archetypes of human behaviour.Life is also different now; not harder or easier, but more instant, a series of moments, the creation of rapid-fire energy. Dowman has grown up inside this. He can parcel his time out, disappear for a bit, maybe make a show of things in the spring.And yes, this is another way of fitting him to a model, laying a lifesize map of future Max Dowman across the present. But I strongly suspect he will be fine, and that unlike so many other things out there he’s pretty well adapted to whatever the future is supposed to look like.Explore more on these topicsArsenalcommentShareReuse this content

title: Premier League news: Carrick brushes aside questions over future, Arteta salutes ‘extraordinary’ Dowman  | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: United head coach believes it will take ‘a lot longer than one or two’ setbacks before he is concerned about his job
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: United head coach believes it will take ‘a lot longer than one or two’ setbacks before he is concerned about his job
Content: Manchester United’s head coach Michael Carrick says: ‘I know what’s expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard.’Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenManchester United’s head coach Michael Carrick says: ‘I know what’s expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard.’Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAThe talkManchester UnitedPremier League news: Carrick brushes aside questions over future, Arteta salutes ‘extraordinary’ DowmanUnited head coach believes it will take ‘a lot longer than one or two’ setbacks before he is concerned about his jobGuardian sport and Press AssociationFri 18 Sep 2026 17.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1.Carrick insists: ‘It’s not a blame game’Michael Carrick says it will take more than one or two defeats before he comes under internal pressure as the Manchester United head coach.United lost 3-2 toBrighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, having led 2-0 at Old Trafford. That followed Sunday’s 1-0 home loss to 10-man Manchester City. United also went down 2-0 at Hull on the opening day of the season and conceded a late equaliser at Everton at the beginning of the month. The results have causedCarrick to come under scrutinyand he was reminded before Sunday’s visit to Fulham that his predecessors, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, were sacked after 30 months and 14 months, respectively, in the job.“It will be a lot longer than one or two games of results [before he is under pressure from United’s hierarchy],” Carrick said: “It’s irrelevant for me. I know the club, I know the role, I know what’s expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard.“In terms of the future and ownership and how long I’ve got, it’s totally nothing, it’s ridiculous to think that way in the position I’m in: it’s just not on the radar. It’s two or three games we haven’t had certain results. We’ve got to perform and we’ve got a lot of games to plan for.”Carrick is content to take ownership of his team’s performance. “That’s why I’m here. It’s my responsibility, I’m fine with that,” he said. “It’s not a blame game. We always search for things to look at and find the blame, sometimes it gets too much. Blame me, it’s no problem, but it’s not about blaming people. It’s about finding solutions. It’s a collective thing. I know where we want to go and we want to get there fast. We don’t like losing matches, but it doesn’t affect what we do next.”The 45-year-old was asked if he needs to show more emotion on the touchline. “I need to show more emotion? In what way?” he replied. “What do you want me to show?”On Friday JJ Gabriel travelled to Barcelona for discussions regarding potentially joining the club, with United understood to have found out via the media despite the 15-year-old being registered with them.On Tuesday Gabriel told United he wanted his registration rescinded because he wishes to join another club. Real Madrid have a firm interest and it is understood Gabriel and his advisers travelled for preliminary talks with Barcelona.Carrick said: “The situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's OK is the important thing."Jamie Jackson2.Dowman takes step up in his strideMikel Arteta has praised Max Dowman’s “extraordinary” transition from schoolboy to Arsenal first-team squad member and backed the teenager to make more of an impact this season.Dowman became the first 16-year-old since Wayne Rooney in October 2002 to score twice for a Premier League club in Arsenal’s victory over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, after bursting on to the scene last year. That was his first appearance of the campaign, having been an unused substitute on four occasions as Arsenal have won all seven of their fixtures.Dowman, who has been training with Arsenal’s first team since he was 14, completed his GCSEs in the summer and he will study for a BTec qualification after deciding against taking A-Levels. Arteta said Dowman’s development was still being carefully managed by Arsenal after a couple of years of having to balance his studies.“It’s not easy,” said the Arsenal manager. “That’s what tells you about the craziness of the age and the environment he still lives in with the demands and the competition he needs to face during the week. But the way he has handled it, him and the family, it has been extraordinary.  If he is here, he has to be here in all conditions and we cannot treat him differently in many aspects.”Dowman is in contention to be on the bench to face Brighton on Saturday as Arsenal attempt to make it eight successive victories to start the season for the first time since 1903. Arteta is convinced more opportunities will come his way sooner rather than later.“That’s the best way to knock on the door: to do it on the pitch, not in the office,” he said. “What Max did the other day, alongside all the players as well, that haven’t played that many minutes, it was really impressive.”View image in fullscreenArsenal’s Max Dowman turns 17 in January when he could go out on loan.Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/ShutterstockPremier League regulations do not allow players under 17 to be sent out on loan but Luton are understood to have registered an interest in Dowman, who was coached by their manager, Jack Wilshere, when he played for Arsenal’s under-18s. Arteta said it was possible Dowman could be allowed to leave in January, by which point he will be 17, but that his immediate future was at Arsenal.“We haven’t really listened to any of the possibilities because we were crystal clear that we wanted to have him in the squad, that we wanted him to be part of the pre-season and then start to see where we are from there,” Arteta said.“We will evaluate every six months, where we are and what is the best thing for him to do and then make the right decision. It depends on a lot of factors – what he needs and what the team needs as well, the availability we have in the squad, the minutes that he is playing and the qualities of those minutes. We have to be open but now the focus is to be here and to impact the team.”Ed Aarons3.De Zerbi grants Tonali time to settleRoberto De Zerbi insists Sandro Tonali is not feeling the pressure of his price tag despite a mixed start to life at Tottenham. The midfielder became the most expensive player in the club’s history when he joined from Newcastle for £92.5m in the summer.De Zerbi made a big play to sign Tonali amid interest from Manchester City and Arsenal, delivering a two-hour sales pitch to his fellow Italian to convince him to move to north London. He outlined how central Tonali would be to his plans and explained what he could expect from Spurs’ fans and the team’s style of football.Tonali has started all four Premier League games this season – in whichSpurs have drawn twice and lost twice without scoring– but has produced underwhelming defensive numbers and created only three chances.De Zerbi revealed he had spoken to the 26-year-old about the weight of the price tag and claimed the player “doesn’t feel the pressure about that”. The Spurs manager pointed out that Tonali took time to adapt in his first season at Milan in 2020 before becoming one of the most sought-after young midfielders in the world once he settled there.De Zerbi said “the adaptation has been not so fast” at Tottenham “but it can happen”, adding: “It is not so easy to change city, to change everything, for the players. Sometimes the adaptation is immediate, sometimes you need more time.”View image in fullscreenSandro Tonali has started all four Premier League games this season, but Spurs are still seeking their first win.Photograph: Chloe Knott/Tottenham Hotspur FC/ShutterstockTottenham’s struggles in front of goal have not been helped by Tonali’s inability to create chances for the forwards. The goalless draw against Everton was the first in 140 games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and following a 0-0 against Nottingham Forest, equalling Spurs’ tally of goalless games in the previous 181 matches. The last time they recorded three or more consecutive goalless draws in the league was 25 years ago under George Graham, when they went to four.It is a remarkable run, especially after a summer spend of more than £300m, that leaves Spurs in 17th going into Saturday’s game against Aston Villa, who have also struggled after a summer of major change.De Zerbi maintained he is happy with Tonali’s performances – even though he believes they can improve – and described him as “a complete midfielder”. “His physical characteristics are to play box to box but he started his career as a playmaker. He’s good enough with the ball, he’s good enough without the ball.”Sam Cunningham4.Calvert-Lewin ‘like a good wine’Daniel Farke said Dominic Calvert-Lewin was “like a good wine” after the in-form striker’scall-up into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad. The 29-year-old has been included in the Three Lions’ squad for their Nations League matches after scoring four goals in six appearances in all competitions this season.Calvert-Lewin was given a standing ovation by Leeds fans as he was withdrawn late on inMonday night’s 4-1 win against Newcastle at Elland Road. “Dominic is like a good wine, getting better by the year,” Farke said. “Physically, he’s on a top level and his pace is more than good enough I would say. He’s a very complete striker.”He arrived at Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in August last year and when asked where he ranked among his best signings, Farke said: “At Leeds, while I’ve been here, we’ve made many top signings on a low budget.View image in fullscreenDominic Calvert-Lewin is a ‘complete striker’, says his Leeds manager Daniel Farke.Photograph: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock“When I think about Joe Rodon, Ethan Ampadu, Ao Tanaka. It’s difficult to compare because as a striker you have a different role. But he’s definitely one of our better pieces of business. If you come as a free agent it doesn’t mean it costs no money because there’s a salary. But we believed in him when perhaps not many were doing this. He also believes in himself and he believes in Leeds United, so I would say he was a perfect fit.”Press AssociationExplore more on these topicsManchester UnitedThe talkArsenalBrighton & Hove AlbionLeeds UnitedCrystal PalaceTottenham HotspurAston VillanewsShareReuse this content

title: Uefa and Concacaf ask Gianni Infantino to give Fifa’s billions to its member associations | Fifa | The Guardian
description: Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani have proposed a payout of at least $10m to each association and want the plan to be considered by the Fifa Council
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani have proposed a payout of at least $10m to each association and want the plan to be considered by the Fifa Council
Content: The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino (right), looks certain to run for re-election despite the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.Photograph: Lee Smith/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe Fifa president, Gianni Infantino (right), looks certain to run for re-election despite the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.Photograph: Lee Smith/ReutersFifaUefa and Concacaf ask Gianni Infantino to give Fifa’s billions to its member associationsPayout of at least $10m to each association proposedLeaders want plan to be considered by Fifa CouncilNick AmesandMatt HughesFri 18 Sep 2026 13.33 EDTLast modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 17.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe presidents of Uefa and Concacaf have written to Gianni Infantino requesting that Fifa release money from its $6bn (£4.5bn) reserves to its member associations, stating that the plan to fund them via thedoomed Fifa Forward Enterprise schemewas unnecessary given the cash pile it is sitting on.Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani proposed a payout of at least $10m to each of Fifa’s 211 member associations (MAs), initially as a one-off during the 2027-2030 commercial cycle. They called for an independent review of Fifa’s financial position and said their own study “raises an important question as to whether the proposed transaction was necessary to deliver greater resources to the MAs”.FA chair Hewitt demands Infantino release records of failed World Cup planRead moreThe proposed $10m would be handed out on top of money committed by Fifa’s existing Fifa Forward programme, which paid each MA about $8m over the previous four-year cycle. In a separate letter to the presidents of the Asian Football Confederation, the Confederation of African Football, Conmebol (the South American federation) and Oceania, Ceferin and Montagliani asked their counterparts to support the motion. Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the AFC president, is expected to send an endorsement of their plan.The leaders intend their proposal to be considered at the next Fifa Council meeting on 15 October, where Infantino is due to face Fifa’s nominal decision-making body for the first time since scandal engulfed his reign.The letter to Infantino states: “Our analysis indicates that Fifa should make at least $10million available to each of its 211 MAs over the 2027-30 cycle for investment in infrastructure and football development – an aggregate of approximately $2.1billion. This would be a one-off release of reserves, over and above the approved Fifa Forward Programme, which would continue in full as already committed.”It points out Fifa’s reserves would not dip below $1.5bn even after that scale of distribution, and says a larger handout could be possible “once a clearer picture of Fifa’s financial position at year-end is available”.Ceferin and Montagliani said Fifa “already has the capacity to deliver substantially more to its MAs from its own balance sheet – without any sale of interests in its competitions, and without asking anything of the MAs in return”.They proceeded to point out that releasing part of Fifa’s reserves would “demonstrate that MAs should not have to choose between development and good governance; between investment and integrity; or between financial support and the ability to consider proposals on their merits. Development is an institutional responsibility of Fifa – not a matter of individual discretion.”While Fifa Forward Enterprise had promised member associations about $40m, half of that sum was an optional $20m payment for those signing up to his plan.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionInfantino remains under pressure to resign but lookscertain to run for re-electionin March. It remains to be seen whether he will face an opponent.Fifa was approached for comment.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Oxford United apologise for launching ‘United 93’ clothing range around 9/11 anniversary | Oxford United | The Guardian
description: Oxford United have been forced to abandon a new range of American sports-influenced merchandise given its jarring association with one of the aircraft hijacked on 11 September
Author: Paul MacInnes
Headline: Oxford United have been forced to abandon a new range of American sports-influenced merchandise given its jarring association with one of the aircraft hijacked on 11 September
Content: The club published an apology that admitted to a lack of understanding of ‘the historical context and associations’ related to the branding.Photograph: Oxford UnitedView image in fullscreenThe club published an apology that admitted to a lack of understanding of ‘the historical context and associations’ related to the branding.Photograph: Oxford UnitedOxford UnitedOxford United apologise for launching ‘United 93’ clothing range around 9/11 anniversary‘Campus Collection’ aimed to mark 1893 club foundingRange pulled from website two hours after launchPaul MacInnesFri 18 Sep 2026 10.18 EDTLast modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 17.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOxford United have abandoned a new range of American style-sportswear after it inadvertently referenced the tragedy of September 11.The League One club launched their new “Campus Collection” on Friday morning but had removed it from sale by lunchtime, after clothing designs were revealed to bear the slogan “United 93”. The U’s immediately published an apology that admitted to a lack of understanding of “the historical context and associations” related to the branding and made “sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused”.“Inspired by the style and culture of American sports,” the club originally trailed the Campus Collection as launching on 11 September of this year, the 25th anniversary of the atrocity that killed nearly 3,000 people. Concerns over sensitivity saw the launch then delayed, but when the online collection was finally made available for sale on Friday, images showed models wearing an NFL-style shirt with “United 93” on the chest, in recognition of Oxford being founded in 1893.United 93 wasone of four domestic passenger jetsseized by al-Qaida terrorists on 11 September 2001. A mutiny by passengers prevented hijackers from using the plane to destroy a government building in Washington DC, and it ultimately crashed into a field, killing all 44 people on board. A film titled “United 93”was also madeabout the tragedy.The Campus Collection was live for approximately two hours on Friday before the webpage was deleted by the club after they realised the meaning of the phrase. “The range was released without understanding of the historical context and associations,” the club statement read. “It should not have reached the point of sale and we take full responsibility for not undertaking proper due diligence.“We have removed the collection with immediate effect and are reviewing our approval processes to ensure nothing like this happens again. Once again, we would like to put on record our sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOpinion was mixed among Oxford fans, with many outraged but others inclined to forgive the error. One user of the Yellows Forum called it a “monumental cock-up that I would expect to be sacked for if I’d signed off on it”. Another wrote: “Whilst not ideal … everyone who sees this realises there’s no malicious intent. Ultimately there was just no consideration to it at all.”Explore more on these topicsOxford UnitedUS sportsSeptember 11 2001newsShareReuse this content

title: Kylian Mbappé leaves Nike after 20 years to sign boot deal with Swiss brand On | Kylian Mbappé | The Guardian
description: The France captain, who will also become a shareholder in the company, said of the move: ‘We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning’
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The France captain, who will also become a shareholder in the company, said of the move: ‘We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning’
Content: Kylian Mbappé’s long-term contract with Nike ended after this summer’s World Cup.Photograph: James Lang/Imagn Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenKylian Mbappé’s long-term contract with Nike ended after this summer’s World Cup.Photograph: James Lang/Imagn Images/ReutersKylian MbappéKylian Mbappé leaves Nike after 20 years to sign boot deal with Swiss brand OnFrance captain also becomes a shareholder in company‘We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning’Matt HughesFri 18 Sep 2026 11.48 EDTLast modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 12.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKylian Mbappé has ended a 20-year association with Nike to sign a boot deal with the Swiss challenger company On.The sports and leisure brand, which has previously focused on running and tennis, is planning a major move into football next year and has also appointed Thierry Henry as its football director.Roger Federer, who also left Nike to join them towards the end of his playing career, is a shareholder of the Zurich-based company. Mbappé will also become a shareholder in On.“From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow’s game,” said the France captain. “I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what’s possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football. We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning.”On is a newcomer to football and this week unveiled its first boots, the Lightspray Prototype, which will be available for the mass market from next year before a move into training kit.Mbappé’s departure, which came at the end of his contract after the World Cup, is a significant blow for Nike, which also lost the Barcelona and Spain star Lamine Yamal to Adidas two years ago. The 27-year-old has been the face of many of Nike’s advertising campaigns.“Kylian’s journey with Nike began when he was nine years old,” the company said in a statement. “Over nearly two decades, we’ve shared moments that shaped the game and he has been an important part of Nike Football. We are proud of what we achieved together on and off the pitch.”Nike and Adidas dominate the football market with their boots worn by more than 40% of players at this summer’s World Cup, according to data compiled by the retailer Fútbol Emotion, with Puma accounting for about 10%.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPrevious challenger brands such as Under Armour, New Balance and Skechers, whose boots are worn by the England captain Harry Kane, have struggled to make an impact on the retail market.Explore more on these topicsKylian MbappénewsShareReuse this content

title: Keely Hodgkinson shows off Catwoman style to steal Athlos London event | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Keely Hodgkinson destroyed a women’s 800m field dressed in a hooded black bodysuit, as Athlos London provided a radically different spin on track and field
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: Keely Hodgkinson destroyed a women’s 800m field dressed in a hooded black bodysuit, as Athlos London provided a radically different spin on track and field
Content: Keely Hodgkinson, in unusual attire, wins the 800m in the Athlos all-female athletics meeting at the StoneX Stadium.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenKeely Hodgkinson, in unusual attire, wins the 800m in the Athlos all-female athletics meeting at the StoneX Stadium.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianAthleticsKeely Hodgkinson shows off Catwoman style to steal Athlos London eventBriton destroys 800m field in hooded black bodysuitMill Hill event more like a rave than an athletics meetingSean Ingleat the StoneX StadiumFri 18 Sep 2026 17.33 EDTLast modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 19.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAthlos arrived in London promising that its all-female spin on athletics would provide a radical departure from the status quo. Long beforeKeely Hodgkinsonstepped on to the track dressed in a hooded black bodysuit – part ninja assassin, part Catwoman – it had emphatically made its point.Throughout the two-hour event, the bassline from the aptly named DJ Trauma carried enough force to make eardrums bleed. The stadium PA’s dial appeared to be permanently stuck on Spinal Tap’s 11. And those who successfully scanned a barcode were then shown dancing and waving on a giant screen.But the youngish crowd largely lapped it up. As Hodgkinson was introduced, the stadium MC told the cheering crowd: “Wait until she comes around the corner, she looks bad, bad, bad. In a custom Nike suit, Keely Hodgkinson!”Keely Hodgkinson reveals how freak canal accident ruined world record bidRead moreSoon the roars had become even louder.Athleticssometimes resembles a vicarage tea party. This was more like a rave. Mill Hill has surely never seen anything like it.Afterwards, the Paris Olympic 800m champion insisted that the suit and its aerodynamic design, which also contained openings for her sunglasses and ponytail, had given her an edge. But she could have been running in a thick duffle coat and she would still have won the $65,000 first prize and Tiffany crown with ease.“I think it’s a mixture of fashion, speed and science all coming together, for maybe the future of athletics potentially,” said Hodgkinson, after winning in 1min 56.40sec, more than 2sec clear of the Swiss athlete Valentina Rosamilia. “We weren’t sure when we were going to wear it, but in hindsight an all-women’s event, which is all about glitz and glamour and putting eyes on women, was perfect.”There was, Hodgkinson acknowledged, a nod to Cathy Freeman’s famous suit worn at the Sydney 2000 Olympics. But she insisted that this was a new version, legal under World Athletics’ rules, and with better technology.“The material, they’ve learned so much about making skin faster, humans faster, there’s so much science behind it that you wouldn’t believe. Technically, with the air drag you’re slower with your hair out, but I was like: ‘That’s a non-negotiable.’”Traditional track and field fans probably would have hated most of the night, which featured just 42 athletes and seven events. And the long gaps between events surely didn’t go down well on TV. But this was designed for a different audience. When Hodgkinson arrived on the red carpet in a baggy tracksuit, for instance, she was accompanied by the sound of dozens of screaming teenage girls.“I wasn’t expecting such a warm welcome, but it was fun,” she said. “My outfit was last minute, but for inspiration, I feel like it’s Liam Gallagher. I’m from Manchester, he’s from Manchester, I feel like I look like him.”View image in fullscreenKlaudia Kazimierska, in 4:19.43, just beats Georgia Hunter Bell to win the mile.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianThe stadium commentary was very different too. As the women’s mile entered the final lap, the stadium co-commentator Kath Merry asked: “Who wants the crown? Who wants the $65,000?” The race was decent, mind, with the Polish athlete Klaudia Kazimierska winning in 4:19.43, just 0.11 ahead of Britain’s Georgia Hunter Bell.Afterwards almost every athlete talked about the fun they had. Several even suggested such events were the future of the sport. But the sober-eyed would have left the StoneX Stadium with plenty of questions.Athlos offered a very generous prize fund of more than $1m for this event. But economically it must have stung. Only about 5,000 tickets, the size of the main stand, were sold. And with the event being shown on YouTube, there was no broadcasting rights windfall.At the moment Athlos appears to be operating on the Field of Dreams principle: if you build it they will come. Perhaps they will be proved correct – especially if the sport’s boom accelerates at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. But, as Michael Johnson’s Grand Slam Track has proved, it is fiendishly difficult to build a viable track and field start-up.Still, the fans saw some fine performances. Given how cold and late in the season it was, times were expected to be slow. Yet in the women’s 400m Marileidy Paulino ran a lightning quick 48.73, with Henriette Jaeger setting a Norwegian national record of 48.78 just behind her. Sha’Clarri Richardson won the women’s 100m in a very speedy 10.80.The night concluded with most of the athletes dancing to Beyoncé’s Run the World (Girls) on the large stage. Athlos isn’t there yet. But it has, at the very least, attracted a few converts.Explore more on these topicsAthleticsKeely HodgkinsonnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football culture | Thomas Tuchel | The Guardian
description: Thomas Tuchel said there are times when he craves greater control but that the adrenaline-fuelled Premier League style remains his best template for success
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Thomas Tuchel said there are times when he craves greater control but that the adrenaline-fuelled Premier League style remains his best template for success
Content: Thomas Tuchel is targeting Nations League and Euro 2028 success after leading England to third place at the World Cup.Photograph: Richard Pelham/Fifa/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThomas Tuchel is targeting Nations League and Euro 2028 success after leading England to third place at the World Cup.Photograph: Richard Pelham/Fifa/Getty ImagesThomas Tuchel‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football cultureHead coach says he must accept lack of control in games‘Deep down, English players … they go for it’David HytnerFri 18 Sep 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 17.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel has admitted there are times when he craves greater control in matches. But the England head coach feels the more chaotic, adrenaline-fuelled nature of the Premier League will remain his template as he targets glory at Euro 2028.Tuchel described his team as “maybe not the most economical to play football” in terms of their habit of constantly playing at full throttle.Theylost to Argentinain the World Cup semi-final in July when they had nothing left in the tank and watched the game slip away after going 1-0 up in the 55th minute. England barely touched the ball thereafter, had no control and were reeled in, Argentina winning with two late goals.Tuchel should listen to ‘the 0.1%’ and learn from England’s World Cup mistakes | Jacob SteinbergRead moreTuchel said he would like it if his team “became for 10 minutes more like Spain” when the pressure was on – a reference to the ability of the world champions to dominate the ball; their comfort on it. Ultimately, though, Tuchel will always play to the strengths of his players, what they are used to, what they have grown up with – even what the fans inEnglandmost like.It may be an internal battle for him because he is a coach who finds a lack of control “hard to digest”. But as Tuchel looked ahead to the next international cycle and the Nations League games against Spain (home), Czechia (home and away) and Croatia (away), he talked of how he wanted to “embrace the chaos”.“I’m just wrestling with myself,” he said. “Even if you control matches in the Premier League, how many English players are there in these teams that really try to control matches? Is this in our DNA? Do we really value control? Is this something that comes easy to us? Or do we go: ‘Yeah, but we’re stuck in midfield, we should go, we should attack.’“I’ve seen [England] training sessions on the very highest level of my career … with a lot of speed and ball speed, physicality, dribbling. So it makes me just struggle … how and when [to seek control]. Because we’re talking about the highest-pressure moments, the semi-final against Argentina, 80% of the stadium is Argentinian. So now can you please become Spain for 15 minutes …”View image in fullscreen‘Do we really value control?’ Thomas Tuchel believes England must play to their attacking strengths.Photograph: Paul Childs/ReutersTuchel was asked whether his team’s attempt to dig in grimly and preserve the 1-0 lead against Argentina was a result of their lack of control. “I would say yes,” he replied. “But I would still say it [controlling football] is not how English fans cherish a match. I don’t think that an English supporter goes to a Premier League match and wants to see a controlled match and 1-0 late on. OK, win always. But it comes with international players playing for the teams that are more open to that.Quick GuideEngland's squadShowGoalkeepers:Jordan Pickford, James Trafford, Jason Steele.Defenders:Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarrod Branthwaite, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Guéhi, Lewis Hall, Ezri Konsa, Tino Livramento, Nico O’Reilly, Jarell Quansah.Midfielders:Elliot Anderson, Jude Bellingham, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Alex Scott.Forwards:Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Eberechi Eze, Anthony Gordon, Harry Kane, Rio Ngumoha, Marcus Rashford, Morgan Rogers, Bukayo Saka.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“Deep down, in the core, English players and the spectators – and this is a beautiful thing – they go for it. They say: ‘Let’s play [for] 6-3 or 4-3. Let’s not play 1-0. We want to put the ball up front.’ There was the famous kick-and-rush in earlier times. There is no heritage of: ‘Oh, let’s control around the middle line. Let’s do a deep buildup and then bring them out.’ It’s just like: ‘Come on. Let’s kick the ball into the opponent’s box and fight with them.’skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Now that I have a tournament as an experience, I feel that this team is ready to fight, is always ready to go. This is the beauty of it. That come the high-pressure moments where we can play better football, where we maybe lack even a little bit of courage or this energy … maybe it’s more going down that route.”It was put to Tuchel that he ought to be able to finesse his gameplan to include spells where the team could retain the ball against elite-level opposition because England have polished players. He said he did not “have the time to coach them” like this. The way Tuchel sees it, he has come into a specific football culture. It is not on him to change it, rather to work with what he has – including the numerous positive traits. Tuchel is not about to push a different game model. “No,” he said. “I know I don’t [do that]. I think it will not suit the characteristics of our players.”Tuchel said he had “mixed” feelings about the World Cup because of the Argentina defeat. He also accepted that his team could have played better across the piece. But he will not allow the second half against Argentina to override the positives and how, after the win overFrance in the third-place playoff, it added up to England’s best tournament finish since 1966.“I have never said it was a big success,” Tuchel said. “I said there were a lot of positives. It was unfulfilled. But why is the expectation so high? When did we last win it? When did we ever win it? Why is the expectation so high that even bringing home a [bronze] medal cannot be acknowledged?”Explore more on these topicsThomas TuchelEnglandnewsShareReuse this content
